title: 需求访谈中礼貌插话澄清审批流程
titleEn: Jumping in to clarify during a requirements interview
scene: 周二上午，你作为 BA 在 Teams 上和财务部应付账款（Accounts Payable）组长 Trent 做需求访谈，了解公司现在的报销审批流程，为新系统做准备。Trent 人很好，但讲话飞快、一说就停不下来，满口内部缩写和澳洲口语，还经常一句话里塞好几个数字和例外情况。
你的目标：① 在他讲太快或信息太多时，礼貌地插话、请他放慢或重复；② 用自己的话复述，确认审批金额门槛、谁来批、有哪些例外；③ 在会议结束前约好后续：你发会议纪要，他补发相关表格和联系人。

facts.v: 现有报销审批流程（current state）
你周四前发 summary；他发 approval matrix

vocab.ex: Could you walk me through what happens after someone submits a claim?
Sorry, can I just jump in there for a sec?
What's the threshold for the second approval?
Anything over five grand, the GM has to sign off on it.
If the receipt's missing, the claim just bounces back to them.

vocab.zh: 变通办法、临时绕开的做法
vocab.ex: So the spreadsheet is basically a workaround?
Are there any edge cases I should know about?

vocab.zh: 痛点、最让人头疼的地方
vocab.ex: What's the biggest pain point for your team right now?
We spend half the week chasing managers up.

vocab.en: off the top of my head
vocab.zh: 凭印象、不查资料随口说
vocab.ex: Off the top of my head, it's about two hundred claims a month.

vocab.zh: 一千（澳元）/ 五千（澳元）
vocab.ex: Anything under a grand goes straight through.
That's a bigger question — can we take that offline?

listening.en: Yeah, how're you going? Sorry, I'm a couple of minutes late — back-to-backs all morning.
listening.sound: how're you going → "how-ya-goin"（=How are you?）；back-to-backs = 连轴转的会议
listening.zh: 你好吗？抱歉晚了几分钟——一上午会议连着开。
listening.reply: Good, thanks. No worries at all — thanks for making the time.

listening.en: So basically it goes to their line manager, then if it's over a grand it goes up to the cost centre owner, unless it's IT, then it's a whole different kettle of fish.
listening.sound: 一句话塞了三层信息；over a grand = 超过一千澳元；a whole different kettle of fish = 完全是另一回事
listening.zh: 基本上先到直属经理，如果超过一千就再上报成本中心负责人，除非是 IT 的，那就完全是另一套了。
listening.reply: Sorry, can I just jump in there? So the second approval kicks in at a thousand dollars — have I got that right?

listening.en: To be fair, half the time they bounce back 'cause the receipt's dodgy or there's no GL code on it.
listening.sound: to be fair → "t'be-fair"；'cause = because；dodgy = 不靠谱、有问题；GL code = 总账科目代码
listening.zh: 说实话，一半时候被退回，是因为收据有问题或者没写科目代码。
listening.reply: That's really useful. Roughly how many claims bounce back each month?

listening.en: I reckon we spend a good chunk of Monday just chasing managers up, it's a bit of a nightmare.
listening.sound: I reckon = 我觉得；a good chunk of → "a-goo-chunk-of" = 很大一部分
listening.zh: 我觉得我们周一一大半时间都在催经理审批，挺头疼的。
listening.reply: So chasing up approvals is one of the main pain points?

listening.en: Off the top of my head, I wanna say around two-fifty a month, but don't quote me on that.
listening.sound: wanna = want to；two-fifty = 250；don't quote me on that = 别把我这话当准数
listening.zh: 凭印象大概每个月两百五十单左右，不过别当准数。
listening.reply: No worries. Would you be able to send me the actual numbers later?

listening.en: Ah, look, that's probably one to take offline, there's a bit of history there.
listening.sound: look 开头只是语气词，不是让你看；take offline = 会后单聊；a bit of history = 有些来龙去脉
listening.zh: 嗯，这个可能得会后单聊，里面有点历史原因。
listening.reply: Sure, happy to. I'll pop it in the summary as an open question.

speech.topic: 说说我在工作中听不懂或没跟上时，是怎么处理的
paragraphs: Today I want to talk about how I deal with meetings when people speak too fast. In my job, I often run interviews with people from other teams to understand how they work. Most of them are really friendly, but some of them talk very quickly and use a lot of short forms and local expressions.

When I first started, I was too shy to stop anyone. I just nodded and hoped I could work it out later. But after the meeting, I often found I had missed an important number or a step in the process. Then I had to send extra emails, and that took more time for everyone.

Now I do things differently. When someone gives me too much information at once, I say, "Sorry, can I just jump in there?" Then I repeat the main point in my own words, like, "So anything over a thousand dollars needs a second approval. Is that right?" People usually don't mind at all. In fact, they often say it helps them think more clearly too.
I also take short notes and write down questions I can't ask straight away. At the end of the meeting, I go through them quickly, and if there isn't enough time, I ask if we can take it offline.
What I learned is that asking for clarification doesn't make me look weak. It shows I'm listening carefully and I want to get it right. Now I feel much more confident in meetings.
speech.zh: 我讲的是开会时别人语速太快我怎么处理。我的工作经常要和其他团队做访谈，大部分人很友好，但有人语速快、缩写和本地说法很多。刚开始我不好意思打断，只是点头，想着之后再弄明白，结果会后常常发现漏了关键数字或步骤，只好再发邮件，大家都更费时间。现在我会说 "Sorry, can I just jump in there?"，再用自己的话复述要点并确认，对方一般完全不介意，还说这样能帮他们理清思路。我也会简短记笔记，把当时没问的问题记下来，会议结束前快速过一遍，时间不够就约会后再聊。我的体会是：请对方澄清不代表能力差，而是说明我在认真听、想把事情做对。现在我开会自信多了。

patterns.en: Sorry, can I just jump in there? ___
patterns.zh: 不好意思，我插一句：___。（换成：I want to check the number / I missed the last part）
所以是 ___，对吗？（用自己的话复述对方的要点）
能带我过一遍 ___ 吗？（换成：the approval steps / what happens next）
我学到的是 ___。（用于总结演讲）

lines.en: Hey, how're you going? Sorry I'm a couple of minutes late, it's been back-to-backs all morning.
lines.zh: 嘿，你好吗？抱歉晚了几分钟，一上午会议连着开。

lines.en: Good, thanks, Trent. No worries at all. Thanks for making the time. Today I'd just like to understand how expense claims work at the moment.
lines.zh: 挺好的，谢谢 Trent。完全没关系，谢谢你抽时间。今天我主要想了解一下现在报销是怎么走流程的。

lines.en: Yeah, too easy. Where do you wanna start?
lines.zh: 好，没问题。你想从哪儿开始？

lines.en: Could you walk me through what happens after someone submits a claim?
lines.zh: 能带我过一遍有人提交报销之后会发生什么吗？

lines.en: Sure. So basically it goes to their line manager, then if it's over a grand it goes up to the cost centre owner, unless it's IT, then it's a whole different kettle of fish, 'cause they've got their own budget and Sandra signs off on everything.
lines.zh: 好。基本上先到直属经理，如果超过一千就上报成本中心负责人，除非是 IT 的，那就完全是另一套，因为他们有自己的预算，所有单子都由 Sandra 批。

lines.en: Sorry, can I just jump in there? That was a lot. Could you say the last part again a bit slower?
lines.zh: 不好意思，我能插一句吗？信息有点多。最后那部分能再慢一点说一遍吗？

lines.en: Yeah, sorry, I do go a bit fast. IT claims don't follow the normal path. They all go to Sandra, the IT finance manager, no matter how much.
lines.zh: 哦抱歉，我是讲得有点快。IT 的报销不走正常流程，不管多少钱都交给 IT 财务经理 Sandra。

lines.en: Got it. Just to confirm, for everyone else, anything over a thousand dollars needs a second approval from the cost centre owner. Is that right?
lines.zh: 明白。确认一下，其他部门的话，超过一千澳元需要成本中心负责人二次审批，对吗？

lines.en: Spot on. And anything over five grand, the GM has to sign off as well, but that's pretty rare.
lines.zh: 完全正确。超过五千的话，总经理也得签字，不过那很少见。

lines.en: Okay, so three levels: line manager, cost centre owner over one thousand, and the GM over five thousand. What happens if something's missing?
lines.zh: 好，那就是三级：直属经理、超过一千的成本中心负责人、超过五千的总经理。如果缺了什么材料会怎样？

lines.en: To be fair, half the time they bounce back 'cause the receipt's dodgy or there's no GL code on it. Then my team has to chase people up, and I reckon we spend a good chunk of Monday doing just that.
lines.zh: 说实话，一半时候都被退回，因为收据有问题或者没写科目代码。然后我们组就得去催人，我觉得周一一大半时间都花在这上面了。

lines.en: Sorry, what's a GL code? I want to make sure I write it down correctly.
lines.zh: 不好意思，GL code 是什么？我想确保记对。

lines.en: General ledger code. It basically tells us which account the money comes out of.
lines.zh: 总账科目代码。基本上就是告诉我们钱从哪个账户出。

lines.en: Thanks. So chasing people up is one of the biggest pain points. Roughly how many claims do you get a month?
lines.zh: 谢谢。所以催人是最大的痛点之一。你们每个月大概有多少报销单？

lines.en: Off the top of my head, I wanna say around two-fifty, but don't quote me on that.
lines.zh: 凭印象大概两百五十单左右，不过别当准数。

lines.en: No worries. Would you be able to send me the actual numbers after the meeting?
lines.zh: 没关系。会后能把准确数字发给我吗？

lines.en: Yeah, I'll get Priya to pull a report. Oh, and there's also a spreadsheet we use to track the late ones, which is a bit of a workaround, honestly.
lines.zh: 可以，我让 Priya 拉一份报表。哦对了，我们还用一个表格跟踪逾期的单子，说实话这算是个变通办法。

lines.en: That's really helpful. Could you send me a copy of that too? Why did the team start using a spreadsheet?
lines.zh: 这很有帮助。那个表格也能发我一份吗？当初组里为什么开始用表格？

lines.en: Ah, look, that's probably one to take offline. There's a bit of history there with the old system.
lines.zh: 嗯，这个可能得会后单聊，和旧系统有点历史渊源。

lines.en: Sure, happy to. I'll pop it in the summary as an open question. We've got about five minutes left. Are there any edge cases I should know about?
lines.zh: 好，没问题。我会把它写进纪要作为待定问题。我们还剩五分钟左右，有没有什么特殊情况我需要知道？

lines.en: Corporate cards. They skip the line manager and come straight to us, but only under three hundred bucks.
lines.zh: 公司信用卡。它们跳过直属经理直接到我们这儿，但仅限三百块以下。

lines.en: Just to check, under three hundred dollars, corporate card spending comes straight to your team?
lines.zh: 确认一下，公司卡消费三百澳元以下直接到你们组？

lines.en: Yep, that's it.
lines.zh: 对，就是这样。

lines.en: Great. I'll send you a summary by Thursday. Could you check it and let me know if I've missed anything? And could you send the approval matrix as well?
lines.zh: 好的。我周四前把纪要发给你。你能帮忙看一下有没有遗漏吗？另外能把审批权限表也发我吗？

lines.en: Too easy. Cheers for that, this was actually really good. Catch you later!
lines.zh: 没问题。谢谢，这次聊得挺好的。回头见！

lines.en: Thanks so much, Trent. Have a good one.
lines.zh: 非常感谢 Trent，祝你今天顺利。

rescue.en: Sorry, can I just jump in there for a sec?
rescue.zh: 不好意思，我能插一句吗？

rescue.en: That was a lot — could you go over that again a bit slower?
rescue.zh: 信息有点多，能再慢一点讲一遍吗？

rescue.en: Sorry, what does that stand for?
rescue.zh: 不好意思，那个缩写是什么意思？

rescue.en: Just so I've got it right, you're saying …?
rescue.zh: 确认我理解对了，你的意思是……？

rescue.en: Would you mind sending that to me in an email after the meeting?
rescue.zh: 你介意会后把这个发邮件给我吗？

checklist: 我能用 "Sorry, can I just jump in there?" 礼貌地打断对方，而不是一直点头
我听懂了 a grand / five grand 这类金额说法，并能复述三级审批门槛
遇到不懂的缩写（如 GL code），我敢直接问它是什么意思
我能用 "Just to confirm … Is that right?" 复述确认至少两次
对方说 take it offline 时，我知道怎么回应并记为待定问题
会议结束前，我说清楚了后续：谁发什么、什么时候发
